author: s. g. nava
title: Reagan Paul criticizes majority party policies and highlights low wind power output in New England
text:
Reagan Paul, a public figure active on social media, recently posted a series of tweets addressing state policy issues and regional energy production. The posts, made on June 9 and June 10, 2026, touch on topics ranging from taxation to the role of renewable energy in New England.
On June 9, Paul wrote: “As you go to the polls today, consider what the majority party has done and will continue to do to our state.
Highest property taxes, highest energy costs…and Nazi tattoos.
Enough is enough.”
The following day, Paul shared real-time data about energy generation in New England: “️Right now at 9:35 am on June 10th, 2026:
ALL of the wind turbines in ALL of New England are contributing only 3.3% of the power to our grid.
Or in other words — only 408 MW of the current system demand of 12,331 MW.
Other contributing resources:
Solar: 5.6%
Refuse: https://t.co/mU55GIC8NE”
Later that day, Paul posted a tweet containing only a link: “https://t.co/zOmjpq4WEu” .
New England has faced ongoing debates over its high property tax rates and energy costs compared to other U.S. regions. According to recent reports, residents have consistently cited these expenses as significant financial burdens ( source ). Additionally, while wind and solar power are part of New England’s energy mix, they contribute less than traditional sources during periods of peak demand ( source ). The conversation around renewable energy’s reliability continues amid efforts to transition toward cleaner sources.
Paul’s tweets reflect broader political discussions within the state regarding fiscal policy and infrastructure investment as voters head to the polls.
